**Issue #4515 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4515: Patch: when the AI foresees the opponent's Activates, it tries every visible card's ability, aimed at its own most valuable card, instead of the first four uses the game lists
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the AI plans a turn, it imagines the opponent's next turn. That includes the abilities on the opponent's face-up cards: a Cannon that deals 7 damage to a unit, a Starship carrying several guns, The Power to Punish. It imagines only four uses, to stay quick. Today those four are simply the first four the game happens to list: one card's ability, aimed at the AI's hero and then at the AI's units from the left.

So with five units out, the AI believes its unit in the far-right lane is safe from the opponent's Cannon. When the opponent shows two such cards, it never imagines the second one firing at all.

Once this is built, the four tries are spread over every such card the AI can see. Each is aimed at the AI's hero first, as now, and then at the AI's most valuable card, so the AI plans around the shot a player would really take. The same fix lets the AI see what its own Starship's second gun is worth. It thinks no longer than before: still four tries.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:598-615`, `visible_activation`, gathers every legal Activate whose source the seat can see. It sorts them by `aim_of` (the seat's hero, then the seat's cards, then the rest) with a stable sort (`// Stable, so each aim keeps legal_actions order.`). Then it truncates to `AI_REPLY.visible_activations`, which is 4 (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:1047`).
- That order is card by card, lane by lane (`crates/engine/src/reduce.rs:924-934`). Within a card it goes ability by ability, then Tribute set by Tribute set, each crossed with every target choice (`crates/engine/src/subsystems/activate.rs:752-800`). Targets list a side's Units in lane order (`legal_selections_for` in `crates/engine/src/play_choices.rs`). So the four tries are the first source's first targets:
  - **Cannon v4** (`stinkyscape-056`, Activate: deal 7 damage to an enemy Unit) facing a full row of five: the tries aim at lanes 1 to 4, so the reply never destroys the Unit in lane 5, whatever it is worth. Lines that put a Unit in different lanes are scored through this same reply, so lane 5 reads as out of the Cannon's reach.
  - **Two visible sources**, or one card with two Activates (a fused card keeps each ingredient's, R3291000, a launched Starship among them): while the first has three or more targets on the seat, its targets fill all four tries and the second gun is never tried.
  - **Turtinator** (`classic-021`, Tribute another Unit and deal its Attack to a Unit or hero): each Tribute set lists its own hit on the hero. With three Units to tribute, the four tries are three hero hits and one hit on the seat's leftmost Unit.
- The same function prices each card's Activate at the decision's root, one card at a time (`price_uses`, `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:2703-2719`, R2564000). So a second ability, or any target past the fourth, goes unpriced there too, for the seat's own cards as for the enemy's.
- The cut has hidden a move before. `tries_the_activation_aimed_at_the_seats_hero_first_so_a_busy_board_never_hides_the_lethal` (`crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`) is why the hero comes first. That settled the hero; nothing orders the rest.
- About twenty shipped cards aim an Activate at an enemy card, all in sets AI decks are dealt from:
  - the Stinkyscape Starship Pieces: Cannon, Beam and Repeater v3 to v5, Jade Launcher and Frost Module;
  - Stinkyscape+'s Arc, Sei, Omura, Vela and Corvus;
  - Core's Heroic Power, and Classic's The Power to Punish and Turtinator.
- This is not #3823 (rejected), which searched the AI's own prompt answers to rank them and spent nodes doing it. This reorders the opponent's tries by a static read and spends exactly the nodes it does today.

## Proposal

In `visible_activation`, order the tries before the cut:

1. Every try aimed at the seat's hero comes first, in legal order, each of its Tribute sets included. This is unchanged, so no lethal that today's order sees is lost.
2. Then come the tries aimed at a card of the seat's, each pick once. A pick is its source, ability, modes and targets; a second Tribute set of the same pick waits. Deal the picks round-robin over the visible sources and their abilities, in legal order: each source-and-ability's best target, then each one's second, and so on. Each source-and-ability ranks its own targets by the seat's worth of the card aimed at, highest first: `unit_worth` under `AI_EVAL` (already imported in `reply.rs`) for a Unit, then the seat's other cards in legal order.
3. Then come the Tribute sets that waited, then every other try, in legal order.
4. Then the cut to `AI_REPLY.visible_activations`, unchanged.

A new switch, `AI_REPLY.spread_activations`, is true by default. Set to false, it gives back today's order exactly, so a test can show what changed and a screen can compare the two. The new order reads only the board the seat sees and its own cards (R185).

§9.9 does not make this decision, so it gets:
- a ruling note in the issue's block, with a test named after it;
- its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`;
- a line in §9.9's reply bullet and in the README's reply paragraph.

A deal screen on the dev set (`cargo jackioh arena --set improve-dev`) is welcome but not owed: scene tests settle it, as R4433000's switches were settled. If one is played, its line goes in the ruling, and only an interval wholly below 0 ships the switch off.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (`visible_activation` and a helper that orders its tries)
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`spread_activations` in `AI_REPLY`)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs` (`mod visible_activations`) and `crates/ai/tests/ai/activations.rs` (the root's price)
- `crates/ai/README.md` (the reply paragraph); SPEC §9.9, The opponent's reply (`spec/09-architecture.md`); `docs/polish/3-ai.md` if it states the order
- `spec/rulings/R<n>.md` and `spec/pending/<issue>.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The opponent shows a ready Cannon v4, and the seat holds five Units with its most valuable in lane 5: `simulate_reply` destroys the lane-5 Unit. With `spread_activations` false it destroys one in lanes 1 to 4, so the test fails without the change.
- [ ] The opponent shows two visible sources, the first able to aim at four or more of the seat's cards: the second source's use is among the tries, and the reply plays it where it is the opponent's best move.
- [ ] A card with two Activates (a fused card, a launched Starship, or a fixture as `tests/ai/starship.rs` builds) has both tried. This holds in the reply and in the root's activation price (R2564000), which takes the better of the two.
- [ ] `tries_the_activation_aimed_at_the_seats_hero_first_so_a_busy_board_never_hides_the_lethal` and every existing reply and activation test pass unchanged.
- [ ] A reply step tries at most `AI_REPLY.visible_activations` uses, and on the same board spends the same nodes with the switch on and off.
- [ ] Two states that differ only in the seat's hidden cards give the same tries and the same decision (R185).
- [ ] The ruling's note, its `r<n>_` test and its pending paragraph are in.
- [ ] These are green: `cargo jackioh spec check`, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh gate` at smoke size.

## Size and risks

Small to medium: about 60 lines in `reply.rs` and `config.rs`, 150 to 250 lines of scene tests, a ruling note and two doc paragraphs. Because it changes the AI, the planner may rate it hard (CLAUDE.md rule 11).

It changes the AI's decisions wherever the opponent shows a targeted Activate, so a test that pins an AI move on such a board may need its expected move re-read.

Two known limits are left as they are:
- For a hit on a card, which Unit a Turtinator tributes stays the first in legal order; its hero hits keep every Tribute set.
- A target is ranked by its worth to the seat, not by whether the hit kills it, since telling would cost a node per try.
```
